correctness.rationale: Synchronous coupling yields strict Lyapunov contraction; the three stationary moments solve a nonsingular linear generator system. An exact two-time semigroup has two distinct negative eigenvalues. The identity (d-k_s)(d-k_f)<0 proves both covariance weights positive. Explicit inversion of the semigroup generator yields the full Green–Kubo integral and the near-infinite reset expansions are algebraically derived. Independent 80-point matrix generator comparisons, 16 quadratures, six large-reset checks, and direct Poisson-reset Langevin simulation corroborate the closed proof. The t>0 restriction is explicit.

originality.rationale: The primary Santra–Das paper contains the coupled model, stationary marginal laws and relaxation of one-time moments, which this result attributes to prior work. Its identified full-text statements do not establish the stationary two-time covariance, two strictly positive modes, Green–Kubo integral, or nonuniform strong-reset excess. Related studies change the reset operator or physical observable; claim-directed published record searches returned no covering title/summary. General linear jump-generator results may implicitly derive these expressions and remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: General linear jump-process theory may implicitly provide the result as a special case, despite no matching explicit statement being identified.

value.rationale: A measurable integrated position observable has excess asymptotic variance even when one-time probe variance agrees at leading order with isolated Brownian resetting. The exact excess factor 1+gamma/2, full relaxation spectrum, and nonuniform fixed-lag bath tail identify a sharp experimentally relevant distinction between one-time and temporal Markovianization; no general downstream theorem is asserted.
